source.section: PIT-ADJ instructions PDF page 3, line 10; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12; Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = IRA distribution (person 0) 40,000.00 + Railroad Retirement benefits (person 0) 30,000.00 = 70,000.00. Federal taxable income = 70,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 additional for age 65 or older = 52,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, single. Line 9 federal AGI 70,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 17,750.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 70,000.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 36,667.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 13 age 65 or older: Table 1 (single) row for federal AGI 70,000.00 gives 0.00 x 1 qualifying = 0.00; line 10 Railroad Retirement benefits, exempt in full = 30,000.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 30,000.00. Line 17 = 70,000.00 + 0.00 - 17,750.00 - 0.00 - 30,000.00 = 22,250.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 52,250.00 - 30,000.00 = 22,250.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 22,250.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 5,500.00 = 82.5 + 3.2% x 11,000.00 = 352 + 4.3% x 5,750.00 = 247.25; total 681.75, to the cent 681.75. The table row over 22,200 to 22,300 gives 682; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 681.75.
